components.role: Given a task lane, the engine finds the best weights for the founder's actual hardware and produces them deterministically: evidence intake whittles candidates to a sourced shortlist (community-measured and reported results; vendor claims are leads, never evidence; dark-web lane under the standing dark-web doctrine, queries normalized); recipes (parents by sha256, algorithm, coefficients, seed, suite, balance rule, environment) are content-addressed data; merge math (linear / slerp / TIES / DARE) runs FP32 in canonical order, CPU path only; the Judge scores suite quality against measured tok/s under the recipe's balance rule with a flagship quality floor; adoption requires proof by reproduction (the headless digital twin — a text spec that becomes an image on command and works a folder's work list down in order — re-runs the recipe to the identical sha256) and a founder tap; pins carry full parentage, inherit the strictest parent license, and load only under a detached ed25519 signature from the offline founder key.

byteCensus.tool: census.mjs (this file — counted in kingmaker-stack code bytes)
byteCensus.methodology: code = lib/ + tools/ + tests/ + root-level .mjs/.py entry scripts; data = corpora/downloads/audit artifacts/archived model sources per component (see dataBreakdown); other = docs and manifests. Exact file bytes, not disk blocks.
byteCensus.scopeNote: Census covers the seventeen stack directories (the original six homes plus the eleven absorbed components inside kingmaker-stack/). The ~18.5 GB knowledge library and model weights are not in these homes — they are data under the same rule and stream post-install in the v0.4.1 design.
byteCensus.payloadRule: The 4.1 payload ships CODE ONLY. Every data byte below streams post-install (library, corpora, models) or is a local artifact that never ships (audit logs, bundle build output, study sources).
